title: Minimum Cost to Separate Sentence Into Rows
summary: Given a string sentence with words separated by spaces and an integer k, split the sentence into rows such that each row contains at most k characters.
statement: Given a string sentence with words separated by spaces and an integer k, split the sentence into rows such that each row contains at most k characters. Words must remain in their original order, and adjacent words in a row are separated by a single space. The cost of a row is calculated as (k - n)^2, where n is the number of characters in that row. The total cost is the sum of the costs of all rows except the last one. Find the minimum possible total cost by optimally placing line breaks.
constraints: sentence contains space-separated words, each no longer than k.
Rows preserve word order, use one space between adjacent words, and have at most k characters.
Each nonfinal row costs (k-length)^2; the last row costs zero.
hints: The cost of a row depends only on its first and last word, enabling prefix dynamic programming.
Let dp[end] be minimum cost through word end; scan possible starts backward until the row exceeds k.
dp[end]=min(dp[start-1]+row_cost), using zero row_cost when end is the final word.
Every layout has a unique final-row start, so the recurrence considers every valid last break and combines it with an optimal preceding layout.
editorial: Every layout has a unique final-row start, so the recurrence considers every valid last break and combines it with an optimal preceding layout.
